knownFor.label: Constitution & Bill of Rights
knownFor.note: The oldest written national constitution still in use.

knownFor.label: Blue jeans
knownFor.note: Riveted denim work trousers patented by Levi Strauss and Jacob Davis.

knownFor.label: ARPANET (early internet)
knownFor.note: The network that grew into the internet.

location.value: Primarily North America: 50 states (48 contiguous, plus Alaska and Hawaii), the federal capital Washington, D.C., and five major island territories.

terrain.value: Atlantic and Pacific coasts, the Appalachian and Rocky Mountains, the Great Plains, and the Mississippi river system. Total area about 9.8 million km² (4th largest).

climate.value: Highly varied, from Arctic Alaska to tropical Hawaii. The Dust Bowl (1930s) was caused by drought and poor farming practices.

resources.value: Huge farmland, timber, coal, oil and gas, and minerals.
resources.source: Foner, Give Me Liberty! An American History (2019)

disasters.value: Hurricanes, earthquakes, floods and droughts. The Dust Bowl, and the 1918 influenza and COVID-19 pandemics.

population.value: 331,449,281 in the 2020 census, and about 341.8 million in 2025: the world’s third-largest population.

urbanisation.value: New York City is the largest city. Rapid urbanisation from the late 19th century.

disease.value: European diseases devastated Native American populations after contact. Later pandemics included the 1918 influenza and COVID-19.
disease.source: Foner, Give Me Liberty! An American History (2019)

migration.value: A nation of immigrants: mass immigration from Europe (19th–early 20th century), and later Latin America and Asia. About 12.5 million enslaved Africans were shipped across the Atlantic overall, around 400,000 of them to the territory of the US.
migration.source: Foner, Give Me Liberty! An American History (2019)

economicBase.value: Agriculture (including cotton grown by enslaved people before 1865), then industry and today mainly services and technology.
economicBase.source: Foner, Give Me Liberty! An American History (2019)

tradeRoutes.value: Atlantic and Pacific trade, and the world’s largest economy for over a century.
tradeRoutes.source: Foner, Give Me Liberty! An American History (2019)

wealth.value: The largest economy in the world by nominal GDP: about $32.6 trillion, roughly $95,000 per person (2026 estimate, Wikipedia infobox).

moneyAndTax.value: The US dollar, the world’s main reserve currency. The Federal Reserve (1913) and federal income tax (1913).
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: United States (checked 5 Nov 2026) (infobox); Foner, Give Me Liberty! An American History (2019)

inequality.value: Gini 41.8 in 2024 (“medium inequality”, Wikipedia). Historic inequality from slavery and segregation.

governmentType.value: A federal presidential republic with separation of powers (President, Congress and Supreme Court) and federalism.

keyRulers.value: George Washington (first president, 1789–1797). Thomas Jefferson. Abraham Lincoln (Civil War, 1861–65). Franklin D. Roosevelt (New Deal, WWII). Many later presidents.
keyRulers.source: Foner, Give Me Liberty! An American History (2019)

succession.value: Presidents are elected every four years (limited to two terms since 1951). Power has transferred peacefully through elections.
succession.source: Foner, Give Me Liberty! An American History (2019)

institutions.value: The Declaration of Independence (1776), the Constitution (1789), the Bill of Rights (1791), and the Reconstruction Amendments (abolishing slavery, 1865).

stability.value: The Civil War (1861–65), when 11 Southern states seceded over slavery. Political and civil-rights struggles, including the Civil Rights Movement of the 1950s–60s.

eliteConflict.value: Party rivalry (now Democrats and Republicans), the Gilded Age power of industrialists, and sharp political polarisation today.
eliteConflict.source: Foner, Give Me Liberty! An American History (2019)

armyAndTech.value: Since 1945, the world’s most powerful military, with nuclear weapons and bases worldwide.
armyAndTech.source: Foner, Give Me Liberty! An American History (2019)

majorWars.value: The Revolutionary War (1775–83), the Mexican–American War (1846–48), the Civil War, the Spanish–American War (1898), both World Wars (entering WWII after Pearl Harbor, 1941), the Korean, Vietnam and Gulf Wars, and Afghanistan and Iraq.

territoryChange.value: Expanded westward by purchase (Louisiana 1803, Alaska 1867), settlement, and conquest of Indigenous and Mexican lands. Acquired Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines (until 1946).

alliancesRivals.value: Rivals: Britain (early), then the Axis and the Soviet Union in the Cold War. Founding member of NATO (1949) and the UN.

inventions.value: The telephone, light bulb, airplane (Wright brothers, 1903), mass production, nuclear weapons, the internet, and personal computers.
inventions.source: Foner, Give Me Liberty! An American History (2019)

scienceEducation.value: World-leading universities and research. The Moon landing (Apollo 11, 1969) in the Space Race.

openness.value: Generally open to immigrants and new ideas, though with periods of restriction (e.g. the 1924 Immigration Act) and exclusion (e.g. the Chinese Exclusion Act, 1882).
openness.source: Foner, Give Me Liberty! An American History (2019)

communicationTransport.value: Canals (Erie, 1825), the transcontinental railroad (1869), the telegraph and telephone, highways, air travel and the internet (ARPANET, 1969).

religion.value: Mostly Christian (65%), 24% unaffiliated, 2% Jewish (Gallup 2025). Freedom of religion and no established church (First Amendment).

languageWriting.value: English (official), with Spanish widely spoken and many immigrant and Indigenous languages.

artsArchitecture.value: Jazz, blues and rock music, Hollywood film, skyscrapers, and global popular culture.
artsArchitecture.source: Foner, Give Me Liberty! An American History (2019)

socialStructure.value: Historically shaped by slavery (abolished in 1865), segregation (Jim Crow) and the displacement of Native Americans. Today a diverse society: 61.6% White, 18.7% Hispanic or Latino, 12.4% Black and 6% Asian (2020).

sharedIdentity.value: The ideals of the Declaration of Independence (liberty, equality), the Constitution, and the “American Dream”. Motto: “In God We Trust”.
sharedIdentity.source: Foner, Give Me Liberty! An American History (2019)

dailyLife.value: From log cabins and farmhouses to suburban houses after 1945; wheat bread, meat and corn; cars in daily life.

neighbours.value: Canada and Mexico, and globally the Americas, Europe and Asia.

ideasReligions.value: Spread democratic and liberal ideas and global popular culture. It was the leading Western power in the Cold War.
ideasReligions.source: Foner, Give Me Liberty! An American History (2019)

colonisation.value: Both: colonised by Britain (Thirteen Colonies from 1607). Westward expansion displaced Native Americans (e.g. the Trail of Tears, 1830s). Overseas territories after 1898.

riseSignals.value: Independence (1776–83), vast land and resources, immigration, industrialisation, and democratic institutions. It was a great power by 1900.

peakPeriod.value: After 1945 as a superpower, and as the sole superpower after the Soviet Union’s collapse in 1991.

declineSignals.value: Not in decline by most measures. Debated challenges include political polarisation, inequality, debt, and the rise of China.
declineSignals.source: Foner, Give Me Liberty! An American History (2019)

outcome.value: Ongoing: a federal republic and the world’s largest economy (HDI 0.938, “very high”, 2023).

sources.value: Census data (since 1790), government records, and extensive scholarship. Checked against Wikipedia on 5 Nov 2026. See also Foner (2019).

overallCertainty.value: High for modern statistics. Pre-contact Native American population estimates vary widely (from about 500,000 to 10 million for the area of the US).
